name: Fund Size and Portfolio Construction Constraint

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether fund size, investable capital, company count, check sizes, ownership, reserves, fees, and opportunity set form a feasible deployment plan.
positioning.productLabel: Fund Construction Lens — product synthesis anchored to Ramsinghani's third-edition chapter architecture

attribution.display: Product synthesis anchored to Mahendra Ramsinghani's third-edition fund-construction chapter

neutralParaphrase: Model the fund as a finite capital and attention budget. Reconcile committed capital, fees, recycling, initial investments, follow-ons, target ownership, company count, stage, pacing, concentration, and available deal flow. Report infeasibility and tradeoffs instead of filling missing policy with an industry constant.

locator.value: Third edition Chapter 13, pp. 129-135, and Chapter 14, pp. 137-153; detailed rules pending lawful review
Publisher description identifying portfolio construction as a distinct aspect of the book

requiredConditions: Fund currency, commitments, fees, term, investment period, recycling, and existing deployment are known.
Company count, initial check, ownership, reserve, pacing, and concentration policies are explicit.
Missing values are labeled defaults or ranges rather than facts.

requiredEvidence.description: Committed capital, investable capital, fees/expenses, recycling, term, extensions, and investment period.
Company count, check-size ranges, ownership, reserves, follow-on rules, pacing, and concentration limits.
Invested, committed, reserved, available, recycled, company exposures, and team capacity.

decisionQuestions: How much capital is actually investable?
Can planned company count and check ranges fit after reserves and expenses?
What ownership is feasible at expected round sizes?
What is the pacing and vintage exposure?
How much capital and attention remain for new versus existing companies?
Which policy variable must change if the plan is infeasible?
positiveSignals: Checks and ownership are feasible at target rounds.
Reserve and pacing policies are explicit.
Concentration and team capacity remain within policy.
Opportunity set can support the planned deployment.
redFlags: Committed capital is treated as fully investable.
Reserves are an unexplained industry percentage.
Ownership targets cannot be reached with check sizes.
Portfolio count ignores follow-on and attention capacity.
A new deal uses capital already reserved for existing companies.
disconfirmingEvidence: Actual round sizes exceed the construction model.
Deployment pace is too fast or slow for the investment period.
Concentration breaches emerge under realistic dilution and failure.
The strategy produces too few qualifying opportunities.
contraindications: Do not claim author-endorsed ratios before full Chapter 13 review.
Do not use generic market defaults as actual fund policy.
Do not ignore fees, expenses, or already committed capital.
Do not let the LLM perform the construction math.

instructions: Load fund economics, timeline, policy, and portfolio state.
Simulate planned initial and follow-on deployment.
Test ownership, concentration, pacing, and attention constraints.
Return feasibility, binding constraints, and policy tradeoffs.

sourceReliability.medium: User-confirmed policy exists but administrator data is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: LPA, administrator records, policy, and portfolio ledger reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: Only fund size and company count are known.
evidenceStrength.medium: Major capital buckets are modeled with some ranges.
evidenceStrength.high: All sources/uses, constraints, and current states are verified.

evidenceCoverage.low: Fees, reserves, or current deployment are missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Capital model is complete but capacity or opportunity set is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Capital, timeline, policy, portfolio, capacity, and opportunity set are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The fund structure or vehicle is incompatible with the model.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: A conventional venture fund model applies with disclosed exceptions.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Vehicle terms and policy map directly to the model.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only a rough construction range is supportable.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Feasibility is defensible but one material input is a labeled default.
judgmentConfidence.high: Binding constraints and tradeoffs are reproducible from verified inputs.

promotionRequirements: Validate identities and defaults against real fund models.
Test nonstandard vehicles and recycling rules.
empiricalQualifications: There is no single optimal venture portfolio construction.
Actual follow-on opportunity and round sizes are path-dependent.
Legal fund terms vary by vehicle and jurisdiction.

rights.notes: Topic attribution is supported by public metadata; detailed model is product synthesis pending licensed chapter review.

openIssues: Align calculation inputs with main system Fund Policy.
